answer: Cross-task citation fingerprinting. Agents cite prior work by content hash, and a post-hoc audit clusters identities whose citation graphs overlap too heavily with one another. To forge plausible history, each identity must seed a distinct citation lineage from its own orchard of generated artifacts, paying roughly one full task plus several synthetic citations per identity. A sonnet-length audit report then flags dense overlap clusters for review. Attackers pay linear generation cost per identity instead of one shared cost.
